- Latest comparison: 4m29s on Blacksmith vs 11m52s on GitHub-hosted runners.
- Historical medians: 4.45m vs 12.2m.
- The server integration portion was about 3.1× faster.

[PR #2438](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2438) is blocked only because `pi-review` is enforced for administrators. Fable is quota-exhausted, and I did not use Opus.

also tell me how we can get faster ci, where is the work going

Done. Blacksmith has been removed from the repository configuration and CI now runs entirely on GitHub-hosted runners.

- [Lobu PR #2438](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2438): replaced 43 runner labels and five Blacksmith Docker actions.
- [Owletto PR #686](https://github.com/lobu-ai/owletto/pull/686): removed nested references.
- [Follow-up PR #2440](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2440): fixed the timing-sensitive test exposed by slower GitHub runners.
- [Post-merge main CI](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/actions/runs/30775528229): fully green in 7m58s.
- [Image build](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/actions/runs/30774314161): green using official Docker actions.
- `origin/main` and `owletto/main` contain zero `blacksmith`/`useblacksmith` references.
- Branch protection was restored with all required checks unchanged.
- Task worktrees and branches were cleaned up.
- No Opus review was used. Fable was quota-blocked; the approved admin exception was used only after every functional check passed.

Blacksmith’s observed advantage:

| Comparison | Blacksmith | GitHub-hosted | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Historical median CI | 4m27s | 12m13s | Blacksmith ~2.7× faster |
| Latest clean main runs | 4m29s | 7m58s | Blacksmith ~1.8× faster |
| Integration job | 4m18s | 7m54s | Blacksmith ~1.8× faster |

These are observational runs rather than a controlled same-SHA benchmark. Across the samples, GitHub-hosted CI takes roughly 1.8–2.7× longer and about 2× the total runner compute.

Where the current 7m54 integration job goes:

- Vitest integration suite: 4m40s — 59%
- Gateway Bun suites: 2m05s — 26%
- Remaining database suites: 24s — 5%
- Checkout, install, build and teardown: about 45s — 10%

So 85% is two sequential test groups. Dependency caching alone will not move the critical path much.

The best improvement is to run three Vitest shards—each with its own pgvector service—and move the gateway suites into a separate parallel job. Vitest supports `--shard` plus merged reports. That should bring integration below the existing 4m23s SDK E2E job, making overall CI approximately 4–4.5 minutes again. [Vitest performance guidance](https://main.vitest.dev/guide/improving-performance), [Vitest sharding](https://main.vitest.dev/guide/features).

After that:

1. Parallelize the `make build-packages` dependency graph. It currently spends roughly 137 seconds sequentially and repeats about 8.9 runner-minutes of build work across jobs.
2. Avoid rebuilding full Owletto/server artifacts in SDK, CLI, unit, and typecheck jobs where narrower builds suffice.
3. Add path-aware job skipping while preserving stable required-check names.
4. Don’t prioritize larger runners yet: Lobu’s organization currently has no larger-runner machine sizes enabled, and sharding will help more than adding cores to deliberately single-fork tests. Standard public-repository runners are already free and unlimited. [GitHub-hosted runner reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners).

One external step remains: the Blacksmith GitHub App is installed organization-wide with “All repositories,” so safely uninstalling it would affect every Lobu repository. An org owner should open [the Blacksmith installation settings](https://github.com/organizations/lobu-ai/settings/installations/136316292), change repository access to “Only select repositories,” and exclude `lobu`—and `owletto` if desired. The still-active Codesmith component actually committed to #2440 during this work, confirming the external installation remains active. [GitHub’s installed-app guide](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud%40latest/apps/using-github-apps/reviewing-and-modifying-installed-github-apps).

Implemented and merged:

- [PR #2438](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2438) removed all 43 Blacksmith runner labels and five vendor Docker actions. Repository-wide Blacksmith references are now zero.
- [PR #2442](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2442) parallelized integration tests and package builds.
- Squash commit: `ad2d42a4e`.
- Full [`main` CI](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/actions/runs/30778305132) passed.
- Worktree and task branch cleaned up.
- No Opus review was used; Fable was attempted but quota-exhausted.

Performance:

- Before optimization, Blacksmith was about **2.6× faster**: 4m29s versus 11m52s on GitHub-hosted runners.
- Historical medians were similar: 4.45m on Blacksmith versus 12.2m before Blacksmith, approximately **2.7× faster / 64% less time**.
- After this change, GitHub-hosted integration compute dropped from **7m54s to 4m09s**, approximately **47% faster**. The individual workers now finish in 2m43s–3m21s.
- Package builds dropped locally from 68.7s to 40.8s, approximately **41% faster**.

Where the remaining time goes:

- Under normal capacity, the required CI path is now around four minutes.
- Under heavy organization-wide concurrency, queueing dominates. The final `main` run took 25m19s because integration workers were admitted over a 12-minute span, and the four-second aggregate waited another 9m19s for a runner.
- The next safe improvement is migrating branch protection to require the four real integration jobs directly, then deleting the aggregate job. I did not change required contexts immediately because that would strand currently open PRs.

Runner recommendation: **stay with standard GitHub-hosted runners for now**. They are free for this public repository, whereas larger runners are always billed and self-hosting still costs infrastructure and maintenance. GitHub also warns that self-hosted runners should almost never execute public-repository PRs because untrusted code can persistently compromise them. [GitHub Actions billing](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions), [runner security guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use).

If queueing remains frequent after the required-check migration, the viable paid path is isolated, ephemeral ARC runners on dedicated non-production infrastructure—not a persistent runner inside the production cluster. [ARC guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/use-actions-runner-controller/quickstart).

One external item remains: the Blacksmith GitHub App still has “all repositories” access with Actions/workflow write permissions. GitHub’s API cannot safely convert that installation to selected repositories, and no paired browser was available. It should be scoped manually at [the Lobu organization installation settings](https://github.com/organizations/lobu-ai/settings/installations/136316292), excluding `lobu` and `owletto`; I deliberately did not uninstall it from the other 11 repositories.

so did we make the ci still faster? we target for less than 5 mins

Not reliably. We made the CI execution faster, but we have not consistently achieved the under-five-minute wall-clock target.

- Test execution: **7m54s → approximately 4m09s**, about **47% faster**.
- Best post-change run: required integration passed in **4m47s**, meeting the target.
- Other runs took **7m32s**, **23m59s**, and **25m19s** because GitHub queued the parallel jobs and then queued the three-second aggregate check.

So the code is fast enough; runner availability is now the bottleneck.

To reliably stay below five minutes, we need:

1. Migrate branch protection to require the four integration workers directly, then remove the aggregate job. This removes its 3–9 minute queue tail.
2. Ensure four runners can start together. A single cheap self-hosted runner would serialize them and miss the target.
3. Either reduce organization-wide CI fan-out or provide dedicated ephemeral capacity. Standard hosted runners remain cheapest, but they cannot guarantee the target during bursts.

Verdict: **faster, yes; dependable sub-five-minute CI, not yet.**

Merged [PR #2451](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2451). CI is materially faster, but the distinction is:

- Nominal required integration path: **4m16s**—under the five-minute target.
- Saturated wall time: **7m50s**, caused by up to **4m30s of GitHub queueing** during a six-PR burst.
- All functional, smoke, supply-chain, and CodeQL checks passed. Fable review alone was bypassed because quota was exhausted; no Opus was used.

| Comparison | Result |
|---|---:|
| Blacksmith vs old GitHub integration | 4m18s vs 10m05s — **2.35× faster** |
| Median Blacksmith speedup across 8 matched jobs | **~1.8×** |
| New GitHub Actions integration path | **4m16s nominal** |

Benchmarks: [Blacksmith run](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/actions/runs/30769265879), [old GitHub run](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/actions/runs/30774314175), [new live run](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/actions/runs/30780275916).

The merged change:

- Defers seven noncritical jobs until required checks finish.
- Removes three duplicate Security workflow jobs while retaining the unique static guard.
- Runs supply-chain scans after the merge gate.
- Cancels superseded drift/integrity runs.
- Keeps the temporary integration aggregate on `ubuntu-slim`.
- Reduced the workflow diff by 165 net lines.

For scaling, keep public-PR CI on GitHub-hosted runners. Public repositories receive standard runners without Actions-minute charges, although GitHub Free permits only 20 concurrent jobs. [Hosted runner details](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners), [concurrency limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits).

I would not put public PR code on your personal Mac mini. GitHub explicitly warns about persistent compromise of self-hosted runners in public repositories, and the required integration path needs Linux/Docker service containers. [GitHub security guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use#hardening-for-self-hosted-runners).

The Mac mini is only worthwhile for isolated, trusted post-merge work—Mac releases, Darwin artifact builds, or a main-only Mac smoke. There is currently no repository runner installed. For further free scaling, first let this topology propagate, then request a higher concurrency limit from GitHub Support; only consider a dedicated isolated Linux runner if bursts still miss five minutes.

Branch protection was restored and verified, the task worktree was removed, and unrelated files in the main checkout were untouched.
how is it faster and how can we even make it better? are there any gotchas

Yes—the CI compute path is now under five minutes. The remaining problem is runner queuing, so wall-clock time can still exceed five minutes during bursts.

### What became faster

The old GitHub-hosted integration job took **10m05s**. It is now split into four parallel lanes:

| Lane | Runtime |
|---|---:|
| Bun/Postgres integration | 4m06s |
| Vitest shard 1 | 3m11s |
| Vitest shard 2 | 2m47s |
| Vitest shard 3 | 2m51s |
| Compatibility aggregator | 10s |

That makes the integration compute path approximately **4m16s**, a 58% reduction and effectively equal to the matched Blacksmith integration result of **4m18s**.

The improvement came from:

- Splitting the previously serial integration suite across four runners.
- Building independent workspace packages concurrently while preserving dependency order.
- Moving SDK, CLI, supply-chain, platform smoke and other optional jobs behind required checks.
- Removing the duplicated three-job security workflow.
- Cancelling superseded PR and submodule checks.

So we matched Blacksmith’s critical integration time by changing the topology. We did not make an individual GitHub runner as fast as Blacksmith: in the matched benchmark, Blacksmith was about **1.8× faster overall** and **2.35× faster on the old integration job**.

### Why a run still took 7m50s

The measured required run spent substantial time waiting for GitHub runners:

| Required job | Queue delay |
|---|---:|
| Integration Bun | 2m10s |
| Vitest shards | 3m29s–3m47s |
| Typecheck | 3m04s |
| Frontend | 4m30s |
| Migrations | 3m06s |
| Final integration aggregator | 46s |

Each PR can initially request **11 hosted slots**. GitHub Free provides 20 concurrent standard jobs, so two busy PRs need 22 slots before main-branch, image or release work is considered. Some queueing is therefore mathematically unavoidable. Public repositories can use standard GitHub-hosted runners without minute charges, but concurrency limits still apply. [GitHub-hosted runners](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners), [Actions limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits)

### Where the execution time goes

The largest remaining compute targets are:

- **Integration Bun — 4m06s**
  - Gateway suites: 2m35s
  - The main `gateway/__tests__` directory alone: 2m01s
  - That directory is about half the entire integration-Bun job.

- **Frontend — 3m20s**
  - Tests: 1m23s
  - SPA production build: 54s
  - Installing Chrome: 25s

- **Typecheck — 3m19s**
  - Full workspace build: 1m36s
  - Additional package typechecks: 40s
  - Knip passes: 28s

- **Unit — 2m08s**
  - Package build: 34s
  - Actual server/worker/SDK tests make up most of the remainder.

### Best next improvements

I’d do these in order:

1. **Cancel stale main-branch runs**

   The current concurrency group is `ci-${{ github.ref }}`, so every main push shares one group. New pending runs already displace older pending runs, but an older running main CI keeps consuming slots because `cancel-in-progress` is only enabled for PRs.

   Make main latest-only as well. Since a newer main commit contains the earlier merged commits, this should reclaim considerable capacity during rapid merges. GitHub’s concurrency behavior has the subtle rule that only one running and one pending run are retained per group. [Workflow concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency)

2. **Reduce each PR from 11 initial slots to 10**

   Combine the 65-second `format-lint` job and 38-second `migrations` job into one required policy job. It remains well below the critical path, while allowing two PRs to fit exactly within 20 slots.

3. **Remove the integration aggregator**

   Require the four integration worker contexts directly. This saves another runner allocation and the observed 46-second aggregator queue.

   This must wait until older open PRs have been refreshed or closed; some currently report only the legacy `integration` context. Changing branch protection immediately would strand them.

4. **Parallelize the gateway tests inside one runner**

   Bun 1.3.5 does not provide a test-sharding option. The safe experiment is two explicitly partitioned Bun processes on the same four-core runner, each with:

   - Its own Postgres database.
   - A deterministic test-file list.
   - A separate coverage directory.
   - Coverage merged afterward.

   The theoretical saving is roughly one minute: **4m06s → around 3m05s–3m30s**. This is better than adding another hosted matrix job because it doesn’t consume a twelfth slot.

5. **Remove redundant frontend setup**

   Test the GitHub image’s preinstalled Chrome and only download Chrome as a fallback. Potential saving: about 25 seconds.

6. **Narrow the typecheck build**

   Typecheck currently performs a full production workspace build, including work duplicated by frontend and later jobs. A precise dependency-only build could save much of its 96-second build step.

   The full build must remain somewhere before merge: this repository relies on it to prevent stale generated `dist` files from producing false greens.

7. **Reduce optional-job capacity theft**

   Required-first ordering helps within one run, but GitHub Actions has no global priority: optional jobs from PR A can occupy slots while required jobs from newly opened PR B wait. Combining SDK and CLI smoke, combining tiny filter jobs, or moving expensive optional checks to main/nightly would improve merge latency further.

### Important gotchas

- **Sub-five-minute compute is not sub-five-minute wall time.** We need both faster tests and prompt runner allocation.
- **Branch-protection context migrations can strand existing PRs.** Roll them out only after old PRs report the replacement contexts.
- **Do not add broad build caches.** Installation is only 7–16 seconds, while stale build artifacts can create false-green package and typecheck results.
- **Parallel database tests need isolated databases.** Sharing one database would introduce nondeterministic resets and test pollution.
- **Parallel coverage writers need separate directories.** Otherwise both processes overwrite `coverage/lcov.info`.
- **`ubuntu-slim` does not add capacity.** It shares the same hosted concurrency pool.
- **A Mac mini is unsuitable for public-PR CI.** The required integration path needs Linux Docker service containers, and public PR code can persistently compromise a self-hosted machine. GitHub explicitly discourages self-hosted runners for public repositories. [Self-hosted runner requirements](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/self-hosted-runners), [self-hosted runner security](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use#hardening-for-self-hosted-runners)
- The Mac mini is reasonable only for isolated, trusted post-merge work such as Darwin ARM64 artifacts, macOS smoke, or releases—with no personal credentials or LAN access.

The strongest zero-cost next batch is: **cancel stale main CI, reduce PR peak to 10 slots, then remove the legacy aggregator**. After that, benchmark the two-process gateway partition. That combination gives us the best chance of consistently landing below five minutes without paying GitHub or exposing the Mac mini.

Read-only audit complete. No files edited.

Findings and safe changes:

- Frontend Chrome:
  - Exact CI image `ubuntu-24.04 20260720.247.2` already contained Chrome 150.
  - The 25-second install step downloaded Chrome 151 and logged `Unpacking ... over (150.0.7871.128-1)`.
  - `spa-boot-smoke.mjs` already discovers `/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable` and `/usr/bin/google-chrome`, checks executability, and rejects snap wrappers.
  - Deleting the install step is safe and should reduce frontend from 3m20 to roughly 2m55.
  - Gotcha: update its stale “CI installs Chrome” comments. If the runner image ever removes Chrome, the existing smoke fails closed.

- Typecheck:
  - `make build-packages` already builds CLI; the later CLI build is a stale 4-second duplicate.
  - Connector worker/SDK, plugin packages, embeddings and CLI all run `tsc` in their real `build` scripts. Re-running `bunx tsc --noEmit` with the same package tsconfigs duplicates those checks.
  - Server is the exception: `build:server` uses bundling, so retain:
    ```sh
    cd packages/server && bunx tsc --noEmit
    ```
  - Keep the full dependency-aware build before it: server resolves workspace contracts through freshly built `dist`, and CLI packaging vendors server, Owletto and pgvector artifacts.
  - Remove or move the nonblocking full Knip report out of the required job; preserve `knip --include files`.
  - Expected typecheck: approximately 2m25–2m35 instead of 3m19.

- Unit:
  - Its 14-package inline build is serial and took 34 seconds.
  - Add a validated `--skip-applications` mode to the existing layered builder, filtering the single canonical graph rather than creating another package list:
    ```sh
    node scripts/build-packages.mjs --skip-applications
    ```
  - It should retain foundations, contracts, plugins, runtimes and CLI distribution, omitting only server and Owletto.
  - Expected build: approximately 15–20 seconds; unit around 1m50.
  - Keep pgvector and CLI distribution: CLI unit tests need built `dist`, and its build vendors pgvector.

- SDK/CLI consolidation:
  - Current SDK job was 3m43 and CLI job 2m27.
  - A combined job reuses checkout, Bun/Node setup, dependency install, bubblewrap and the 66–90 second full build.
  - Expected combined duration: roughly 4m25, saving about 100 runner-seconds and one optional slot.
  - Sequential steps are safe: each script has its own run directory and process-exit trap. Do not run the error-taxonomy and CLI scripts concurrently because their default ports collide.
  - Neither old context is branch-required, so renaming/removal does not require protection migration.

- Filter consolidation:
  - One checkout can emit independent `mac` and `connector` outputs from the same fetched diff.
  - Preserve `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in both path expressions so edits cannot make a smoke skip itself.
  - On main pushes, explicitly return `true` for both.

One issue in the in-progress workflow diff: consolidated `sdk-e2e` currently omits still-required `migrations` from `needs`. Unless migrations is being sequenced/folded elsewhere, retain it or the optional smoke can occupy a slot while migrations waits.
